We deliver award-winning services to customers across the country, providing advanced metering technology for electricity, gas, and water, alongside highly accurate energy data collection services. Our commitment to innovation and excellence has established us as a trusted partner in the energy sector, supporting our clients with reliable and efficient solutions that meet the evolving demands of the industry. About The Role The purpose of this role is to own and manage the Azure platform on which IMServ's Astral products are built, tested, and operated. This role is critical in enabling the delivery of highly scalable, secure, multi-tenant SaaS software to clients worldwide. As one of two DevOps Engineers, you will share responsibility for the entire path to production, including managing Azure environments, CI/CD pipelines, releases, security, and cost management. You will work within our Scrum teams, collaborating closely with Software Engineers, Testers, and the Technical Architect. Your primary focus will be to ensure the platform's stability, security, and efficiency throughout the product lifecycle, supporting the seamless deployment and operation of our services. Qualifications Essential qualifications include over five years of experience managing production Azure environments, with a strong understanding of App Services, Azure SQL, storage, and networking fundamentals. Candidates should have a proven track record in building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps (YAML), including artifact management, controlled build configurations, and security gates. Proficiency in infrastructure as code (Bicep, ARM, or Terraform) and scripting in PowerShell and Azure CLI is required. A solid understanding of secure-by-default platform design principles such as Key Vault, managed identities, RBAC, and least privilege is essential. Experience in monitoring, backup, disaster recovery, and incident response for live services is also necessary. Familiarity with Agile SCRUM methodologies and SQL Server management for environment data is highly desirable. Certifications such as AZ-104 or AZ-400 are advantageous, along with experience supporting Azure services like Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions, or Azure Data Factory. Knowledge of C#/.NET and enterprise security requirements will be beneficial for this role. Responsibilities Environment Management: Provision, configure, and maintain the Astral environment estate across development, testing, UAT/load, and production environments. Ensure environments are consistent, reproducible, and well-documented using infrastructure as code. Manage environment refreshes and test data in compliance with data protection policies. CI/CD Pipelines: Develop, maintain, and enhance Azure DevOps build, test, and release pipelines. Incorporate artifact management, controlled build configurations, and automated quality and security gates. Streamline deployment processes by consolidating per-client pipelines into a unified multi-tenant deployment pathway. Release Management: Plan and execute deployments across the environment chain, including rehearsed rollback procedures for each release. Support product go-lives and maintain a transparent release calendar to ensure smooth delivery. Security and Access: Manage secrets and certificates via Azure Key Vault, oversee role-based access control, and enforce least privilege policies across the platform. Collaborate with IT security teams on audit remediation and security release planning. Monitoring, Reliability, and Recovery: Own observability tools such as Application Insights and Log Analytics. Implement alerting, backups, and disaster recovery procedures, including periodic testing. Lead incident response efforts and conduct blameless root-cause analysis to prevent recurrence. Cost Management: Monitor and optimize Azure spend across different environments and clients. Right-size resources based on usage patterns and report on key cost drivers to ensure efficient budget management. Documentation and Knowledge Sharing: Maintain up-to-date runbooks, environment documentation, and configuration records. Document work promptly to eliminate single points of failure and facilitate knowledge sharing within the team. Community Membership: Actively participate in Scrum ceremonies, the wider Product Engineering community, and team events. Support colleagues by quickly resolving environment and pipeline issues to maintain continuous delivery momentum. Benefits 28 days' holiday plus Bank Holidays Buy & sell annual leave scheme Up to a 10% bonus Enhanced salary sacrifice pension scheme Life assurance cover up to 6 times salary Simply Health plan with upgrade options Car salary sacrifice scheme (Length of service and T&Cs apply) Equal Opportunity (in last) At IMServ Europe Ltd, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to do their best work. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, experiences, and communities. We believe that a diverse team brings fresh perspectives, enhances collaboration, and enables us to deliver the highest quality service to our customers. If you are interested in this role but do not meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We reserve the right to close the position early if suitable candidates are found.

review_candidates.job_function: Science, Information Technology, and Customer Service
review_candidates.description: Job Description Organizations don't innovate; people do. As part of our digital transformation business, you’ll help clients unlock innovation, embrace the future, and change communities for good. Who are we looking for? We are seeking an experienced Software Development Manager to lead GHD's global delivery of workflow, automation, and internal software solutions. This role is responsible for managing a compact global team of internal and third-party development squads, ensuring approved work is effectively planned, delivered, released, and supported at enterprise scale. You will oversee team performance, delivery capacity, and implementation consistency while driving best practices across software development, CI/CD, cloud platforms, data integration, and operational excellence. The role plays a key part in building a scalable, predictable delivery model across Microsoft Azure, Power Platform, and Microsoft Fabric. The role can be based in our Waterloo or Toronto office. Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office, three days a week, to contribute, connect, and excel in our vibrant environment. Working with an energetic and high-performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in: Delivery Leadership Lead a compact global delivery organization of 3 to 5 internal development squads, plus third-party developer squads where work is delivered through agreed statements of work. Manage squad performance through internal team leads and vendor delivery leads, with attention to throughput, predictability, cycle time, quality, and support readiness. Define a delivery model that can scale without relying on informal escalation paths or individual heroics. Set operating rhythms for planning, execution reviews, release readiness, delivery reporting, and escalation management. Implementation Planning & Delivery Control Convert formally identified demand into implementable delivery plans with clear scope, assumptions, dependencies, and support expectations. Balance approved work against squad capacity, platform constraints, production support, third-party delivery commitments, and active delivery priorities. Make implementation sequencing, delivery trade-offs, and SOW execution risks visible to partner groups and stakeholders. Maintain a clear view of delivery status, risks, blockers, release readiness, and third-party delivery progress across the squad portfolio. Engineering Quality & Release Readiness Oversee implementation from technical discovery through build, release, adoption, and transition into support. Standardize how internal and third-party squads clarify requirements, estimate work, design solutions, test changes, and prepare releases. Build quality controls into the delivery workflow, including review, testing, documentation, operational readiness, and release acceptance. Define and track delivery metrics such as throughput, cycle time, escaped defects, rework, predictability, support load, and release reliability. Platform, Architecture & Delivery Standards Ensure delivery aligns with approved platform, architecture, data, security, and engineering standards. Set expectations for standard tooling and delivery patterns, including Jira, GitHub or Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, Azure services, Power Platform, and Microsoft Fabric where applicable. Partner with Architecture and Platform leads to apply consistent design patterns across workflow, automation, and internal software solutions. Escalate exceptions where delivery requirements conflict with standards, platform constraints, security expectations, architecture guidance, or long-term maintainability. Vendor & Stakeholder Delivery Management Help shape third-party statements of work so scope, assumptions, deliverables, acceptance expectations, and support responsibilities are clear. Manage third-party developer squads against agreed SOWs, including progress, risks, blockers, quality expectations, and delivery commitments. Maintain working relationships with service lines, Platform teams, Architecture, Support, Delivery Transformation, delivery squads, and third-party delivery partners. Communicate delivery status, risks, constraints, and decision points in a way that is clear to both technical and business audiences. What you will bring to the Team: Essential Experience managing multiple software delivery squads through team leads, including internal teams and third-party development squads working against statements of work. Strong software development background, with practical experience in modern languages such as Python or Node.js and enough technical depth to guide delivery decisions. Hands-on experience across the software delivery lifecycle, including requirements clarification, design, development, testing, release management, and operational support. Practical experience with CI/CD tooling, GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps Pipelines, cloud deployment on Microsoft Azure, and delivery tracking in Jira. Experience with Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Automate and Power Apps, and a working understanding of Microsoft Fabric. A clear point of view on engineering quality, including review discipline, testing standards, defect reduction, release readiness, and supportability. Experience with build-versus-buy analysis and third-party delivery planning, including technical fit, SOW scope, implementation effort, support model, cost, and long-term maintainability. Strong communication and leadership skills, including the ability to operate in ambiguity, clarify technical and business constraints, align stakeholders, and keep squads accountable for outcomes. Preferred Experience delivering automation or workflow solutions at enterprise scale. Experience operating in globally distributed delivery environments. Exposure to enterprise architecture standards and platform-led delivery models. Experience working across both low-code and custom software delivery models. The salary range for this position is: $120000 to $160000 The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for GHD locations in its major city centres. Ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At GHD, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications, and work location. review_candidates.description: Job Description - Lead Solutions Engineer The Lead Solutions Engineer is a technical expert and trusted advisor driving Acquia’s growth across the Japan market. Operating at the intersection of business strategy and technical architecture, this role is primarily focused on winning new-logo business, while also driving cross-sell and expansion across the Acquia Digital Experience Platform (DXP) portfolio. Working hand-in-hand with Account Executives and, critically, Acquia’s partner ecosystem — through which nearly all new business in Japan is sourced — the Lead Solutions Engineer turns customer challenges into compelling solutions that deliver demonstrable business value and substantial revenue growth. Key Responsibilities Strategic Account Growth & Cross-Sell New Logo Acquisition: Be the technical lead partnering with Account Executives and channel / SI partners to identify, qualify, and win new-logo opportunities across Japan — the primary focus of the role. Cross-Sell & Expansion: Identify and accelerate cross-sell and expansion opportunities within strategic accounts where Solutions Engineering support adds value, mapping Acquia’s DXP portfolio to each client’s future-state digital roadmap. Business Value Alignment: Drive a value-based approach by translating solutions into clear, quantifiable business outcomes and return on investment for both technical and business stakeholders. Trusted Technical Advisor: Serve as the technical contact for client stakeholders, providing guidance on digital strategy, cloud adoption, and DXP trends across their technical and business teams. Solutions Architecture & Governance Technical Discovery: Lead the technical discovery, design, and presentation of DXP solutions tailored to each customer’s context and business priorities. Custom Proofs: Design and execute impactful custom demonstrations and Proof-of-Concepts (PoCs) that clearly illustrate the business value of the Acquia platform. Competitive Positioning: Position Acquia against key competitors through strong discovery and a clear point of view on fit, reinforcing Acquia’s unique value. Partner Enablement & Market Presence Partner Enablement: Enable partners at the pre-sales layer — coaching their teams to position and present Acquia products confidently in their own pitches, both one-to-one and at events. Market Presence: Represent Acquia at industry events, webinars, and community gatherings, proactively creating opportunities and visibility across the Japan market. Product Feedback Loop: Serve as a feedback loop to Acquia’s Product and Engineering teams, synthesizing insights from the Japan market to help shape positioning and priorities. Required Skills and Qualifications Experience: Proven experience in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or pre-sales role, or a strong, deeply technical Account Executive ready to operate in a Solutions Engineering capacity. What matters most is the ability to understand a customer’s business and translate it into the right solution. DXP Expertise: Experience selling or pre-selling an enterprise CMS / DXP, or a comparable SaaS platform — vendor-agnostic. Strong understanding of CMS, personalization, and modern digital experience concepts (Drupal a plus, not a requirement). Technical Foundation: Solid working knowledge of modern web architectures and how DXP / web applications are deployed on a major public cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including APIs and security fundamentals. Partner & Channel: Proven ability to work with and through partners / channel to source and win business — central to this role, as nearly all new-logo ACV in Japan is partner-sourced. Communication: Strong presentation and demonstration skills, with the ability to lead both the technical and the business conversation with customers and partners. Language: Native-level Japanese and business-level English — leading customer and partner discussions in Japanese (including written RFP / PoC work) and collaborating with a UK / EMEA-based team in English. Ways of Working: A self-starter who works with autonomy as the dedicated Solutions Engineering presence for the region, acting on sound judgment while maintaining strong visibility with manager and team, and with a genuine appetite for continuous learning. Desired (Extra Credit) Proven track record of success working within a named global or strategic account program. Experience with a major programming language and hands-on ability to build technical prototypes. Published articles, white papers, or presentation experience at major industry conferences. Acquia DNA & Culture This is a remote, Japan-focused role for a self-starter who thrives on high-impact work and enjoys operating with autonomy. The ability to work across time zones with a collaborative, virtual team is essential. Occasional travel within Japan to engage customers and partners is expected; coverage beyond Japan is possible as an upside but is not a requirement.
